outcome: Growth and development of craniomaxillofacial structure
Size of nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal airway
A/N value of nasopharyngeal lateral X-ray images
cohort: The study included 56 children with adenoid hypertrophy (observation group) and 42 healthy children (control group) who visited the Hebei Eye Hospital during the same period.
finding: Adenoid hypertrophy can significantly affect the size of the nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal airway, change children's respiratory mode and respiratory function, and lead to craniomaxillofacial and oral malformations, thereby affecting their normal growth and development.
cross-section timing: Clinical data were retrospectively analyzed from children who visited the Hebei Eye Hospital during the same unspecified period.
